transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve just been feeling worn down most of the time. Even if I get a full night’s sleep, I still feel tired, and after getting through work and dealing with the clutter at home, I don’t really have much left for anything else.
Do you find yourself enjoying activities or hobbies that you used to like?

Not really like I used to. Most days there’s just this low, gray feeling in the background. I can still go to the lab and talk to people, but things like baking or checking the telescope don’t feel as exciting or light anymore.
Do you still find pleasure in social interactions with friends and family?
I’m not sure. I mean, I still like seeing people I’m close to, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it feels pleasurable exactly. It’s more just... okay, I guess.
Do you feel like you're able to experience pleasure or happiness at all lately?
I guess I’m not really sure. I do have moments that are okay, maybe even a little nice, but I don’t know if I’d call it happiness exactly. It just feels more muted than it used to.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?
I don’t think so, not often. I might second-guess myself sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed a lot of guilt or blaming myself.
Can you think of anything recently that you've looked forward to or felt enthusiastic about?

Not much, honestly. I still do things—go to the lab, talk to people—but most days there’s kind of this low, gray feeling in the background. Even things I used to get excited about, like baking or checking the telescope, just don’t really feel light or fun the way they used to.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change either way, I don’t think. My appetite seems pretty much the same.
Have you had trouble concentrating on things lately?

Yes, a bit. Things that used to feel pretty straightforward take me longer now. Like revising a grant paragraph, or even picking materials for a home repair—I’ll get stuck on small decisions, reread things, second-guess myself. It’s like my mind is moving slower than it should.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I don’t think I’m moving or talking much slower than usual, and I wouldn’t say I feel restless like I can’t sit still.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're not a good person?
I don’t think so. I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or like I’m a bad person.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been a little over two years, I think. It started not long after we moved into our older house, and since then it’s just kind of been my baseline.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?
Not really. My weight’s been pretty stable as far as I can tell.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live or wishing you were dead?
No, I haven’t had thoughts like that. I get down, but I don’t wish I was dead or not alive.
Would you say your low, gray feeling is present most of the day or is it more variable?

It’s there most days, pretty much running in the background. I can still go to the lab and talk to people and get through things, but I don’t really feel light or excited about stuff like baking or checking the telescope the way I used to.
Would you describe your current feelings and experiences as consistently affecting nearly every aspect of your daily life?

I wouldn’t say every aspect, no. I’m still getting my lab work done. But it does slow me down—grant drafts take longer than they should, and even routine project decisions feel harder to get through. At home, I’ve kind of stopped keeping up with the baking, the bonsai, and the telescope plans that used to give my downtime some structure.
Has this low, gray feeling you've described been continuous over the past two years, or have you had periods where it lifted and then returned?
It’s been pretty continuous. I’d say that low baseline started shortly after we moved into the older house, a little over two years ago, and it hasn’t really fully lifted since then.
Would you say that this low, gray feeling has been severe enough to significantly impair your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

I wouldn’t say it’s made me unable to function, but it does get in the way. I’m still getting my lab work done, but grant drafts take noticeably longer, and even routine project decisions feel harder than they should. And at home, I’ve stopped keeping up with things like baking, the bonsai, and the telescope plans that used to give my downtime some structure.
